extracted.intended_audience: Medicare-regulated providers and program administrators (eligible hospitals, CAHs, LTCHs, OPOs/HCLs), and stakeholders preparing comments or ensuring compliance with the proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural rules for information collection burden estimates, measure adoptions/removals, and certain appeals/hearing procedures in the FY2027 IPPS/LTCH proposed rule. Targets Medicare providers and program administrators responsible for reporting, cost estimation, and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of BLS median hourly wages and doubling for overhead/fringe
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of calculating costs associated with collection of information requirements, median hourly wages from the BLS (May 2024 National Occupational Employment and Wage Estimates) are obtained and 'To account for overhead and fringe benefits, we have doubled the hourly wage.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: medical records specialists median $27.53 → wage plus benefits $55.06; administrative assistant estimated $43.82 (used in LTCH HCP COVID-19 burden calc). This doubling (100% add) is used consistently unless otherwise specified; treated as a rough but reasonably accurate estimation method. If BLS updates rates before final rule, CMS will maintain the wage rates used in the proposed rule for burden calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation time assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Time required for eligible hospitals and CAHs to complete simple attestations is assumed and used in burden estimates (e.g., 30 seconds for some attestations, 1 minute for others).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific assumptions: Unique Device Identifiers for Implantable Medical Devices attestation—30 seconds (0.5 minutes); ONC Direct Review attestation—1 minute (0.0167 hours); optional ONC-ACB Surveillance attestation—1 minute. These per-entity per-year times are multiplied by the number of eligible entities to estimate total burden and cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: eCQM reporting burden per eCQM
rubrics_metrics.description: The currently approved information collection burden per reported eCQM is 10 minutes (0.167 hours) per eligible hospital or CAH per quarter, or 40 minutes (0.67 hours) annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compute burden increases when measures become mandatory or when the set of required/self-selected eCQMs changes. Example: adding 3 eCQMs → 10 minutes/eCQM × 3 eCQMs × 4 quarters = 120 minutes (2 hours) per CAH annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting only electronic submission burden where patient data already entered into EHRs
rubrics_metrics.description: For eCQMs and measures where patient data are already entered into EHRs as part of clinical practice, CMS accounts only for the time associated with electronically submitting data to CMS in burden estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS assumes no additional information collection burden for entry of Unique Device Identifier information into EHRs where those data are already recorded under other regulations (e.g., 21 CFR 821.30).

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimating number of respondents for burden scaling
rubrics_metrics.description: Burden and cost estimates are scaled by CMS's estimate of eligible reporting entities (e.g., 3,150 eligible hospitals and 1,400 CAHs = 4,550 respondents for the Promoting Interoperability Program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the most recent available program data (here, EHR reporting period in CY 2024) to estimate respondent counts for calculating total hours and dollars; maintain the counts used in the proposed rule unless otherwise updated in a final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite wage calculation for mixed-staff tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a task is completed by a mix of staff types, CMS may create a composite cost estimate by weighting adjusted hourly wages equally or per assumed staffing mix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: for Patient/Resident COVID-19 Vaccine measure, assumed equally by RN and LPN/LVN → composite = (adjusted_RN_wage × 0.5) + (adjusted_LPN_wage × 0.5) = $78.16/hr. Adjusted wages use BLS medians doubled for fringe/overhead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden estimation arithmetic (hours × wage × number of entities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total annual burden hours and costs are calculated by multiplying per-entity time estimates by the number of entities and the wage-plus-benefits rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from text: removal of HCP COVID-19 measure → reduction of 12 hours per LTCH × 318 LTCHs = 3,816 hours; cost decrease $525.84 per LTCH (12 × $43.82) → $167,217.12 total. Show intermediate steps and reference the OMB control number under which burden is accounted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates and applicability for measure adoptions/removals
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed adoptions and removals of measures and attestations specify the reporting period or fiscal year when changes would take effect (e.g., beginning with CY or FY 2027, 2028, or 2030 reporting periods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: removal of HCP COVID-19 Vaccine measure and Patient/Resident COVID-19 Vaccine measure effective beginning with FY 2028 LTCH QRP; Unique Device Identifiers measure beginning with EHR reporting period in CY 2027; certain eCQMs adopt beginning with CY 2028 and may become mandatory after two years of self-selected reporting (timing spelled out per measure). Use these effective periods when calculating burden impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy to make Hospital Harm eCQMs mandatory after two years self-selected reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to modify eCQM reporting/submission requirements so Hospital Harm eCQMs (that are not already required) would become mandatory after two years of self-selected reporting beginning with the CY 2028 reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies only to Hospital Harm eCQMs not already required. Example timeline: measures adopted as self-selected eCQMs beginning CY 2026 would become mandatory beginning CY 2028 (or, for measures adopted later, mandatory two years after self-selection start). Use this policy to project future burden increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: No change to information collection burden when alternative measures remain available
rubrics_metrics.description: When a removed measure is one of multiple alternatives under an objective and remaining alternatives still satisfy reporting obligations, CMS does not propose a change to information collection burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: removal of 'Support Electronic Referral Loops by Sending Health Information' and '...Receiving and Reconciling' measures—because eligible hospitals/CAHs could still report HIE Bi-Directional Exchange or TEFCA measure, no burden change proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: LTCH QRP noncompliance penalty standard
rubrics_metrics.description: As required by section 1886(m)(5)(A)(i) of the Act, an LTCH that does not meet the requirements of the LTCH QRP for a fiscal year will receive a 2-percentage point reduction to its otherwise applicable annual update for that fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory penalty informs the stakes associated with LTCH QRP reporting and thus the significance of burden/cost estimates tied to measure removals or additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: IOPO/HCL Medicare cost report burden and wage calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Burden hours for OPOs/HCLs to complete ongoing data gathering and Form CMS-216-94 are estimated; current average burden per OPO/HCL is 45 hours (30 hours recordkeeping + 15 hours reporting); proposed additional reporting burden estimated at 10 hours per OPO/HCL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wage example: BLS median for Category 13-2011 (accounting and audit professionals) $39.27; add 100% to account for fringe and overhead → $78.54/hr. Multiply by additional hours (10) to determine per-entity additional annual reporting cost ($785.40). Multiply by number of entities (94) for total cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals/hearing amount in controversy threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: With the exception of an IOPO or histocompatibility laboratory, the amount in controversy (as determined in accordance with §405.1839) must be at least $1,000 but less than $10,000 to qualify for a contractor hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IOPOs and histocompatibility laboratories are subject to the different amount in controversy requirement specified in §413.420(g). This threshold is a jurisdictional criterion for contractor hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for filing contractor hearing requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the provider qualifies for a good cause extension under §405.1813, the date of receipt by the contractor of the provider's hearing request must be no later than 180 days after the date of receipt by the provider of the final contractor or Secretary determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers should ensure timely filing within 180 days or seek a good cause extension to avoid dismissal; IOPOs and histocompatibility laboratories remain subject to §413.420(g) provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good cause extension review and finality rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision denying an extension request under §405.1813 and dismissing the appeal is final and binding unless reviewed by a CMS reviewing official, reviewed by the Administrator, or reopened and revised by contractor hearing officer(s). A decision granting an extension is not subject to immediate review but may be examined during later reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific review paths: (i) CMS reviewing official review per §405.1834(b)(2)(i); (ii) Administrator review; (iii) reopening/revision by contractor hearing officer(s) per §§405.1885–405.1889. Decisions granting extensions can be examined during CMS reviewing official's review of final jurisdictional dismissal decisions or final hearing decisions, or during Administrator review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewability of contractor hearing officer jurisdictional findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Final jurisdictional findings and jurisdictional dismissal decisions by contractor hearing officer(s) are subject to the CMS reviewing official procedure and the possibility of Administrator review; jurisdictional findings are not subject to further administrative review except as provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jurisdictional dismissal decisions are final and binding unless: (i) reviewed by a CMS reviewing official; (ii) subsequently reviewed by the Administrator; or (iii) reopened and revised by contractor hearing officer(s) per §§405.1885–405.1889.
